hook_text: Can you roll your tongue? Stand against the wall. Your class is about to become a science experiment.
clip_script: Everyone in your class got half their genes from their mother and half from their father, shuffled into a brand-new mix. That is why no two of you are the same. Let's measure it. Shoes off, back flat against the wall, book on your head, read at eye level. Same way for everyone, numbers instead of names, and no teasing allowed. Now graph it. Heights change smoothly, so the bars touch, and you get a hill: most of the class in the middle, a few very short or very tall. That is continuous variation. Now tongue rolling: can or can't, nothing in between. Separate bars. Discontinuous variation. Twenty-one out of thirty? Twenty-one divided by thirty is seventy per cent. Real data, real science, all from your own class.
visual_style: Whiteboard class line-up against a measuring wall; tally marks turning into a hill-shaped histogram; two separate bars for tongue rolling with 70% labelled.
pacing: Quick genetics opener, a step-by-step measuring routine, two snappy graph reveals.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the survey with your own class.
